doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: Garnett Brown, Herbie's classical concert and Ahmad Jamal's early classical playing
summary: He praises Garnett Brown and Herbie Hancock and Ahmad Jamal's classical background.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: tremendous, we call him Tut, King Tut, and he’s like number one in California. He knows a lot about the college game. He’s always renting TVs and videos and stuff. But Herbie did this classical type thing with Lang Lang this [inaudible] series thing. It was overwhelming. Because Herbie, well he was a Mozart major. But anything he puts his mind to do when he’s going to do it, he’s going to do it extremely well. That’s why I say you know what I told you, Keith Jarrett did the Goldberg Variations and the classical musicians said wow, gee whiz. Ahmad Jamal was playing Lizst etudes when he was eleven years old with the Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra. He never talks about it. So the list goes on and on and on you know.
